$comment: The benchmark manifest. This file is the single authored declaration of what the benchmark contains; every count here is re-derived from the loaded case files by loadBenchmark() and cross-checked, so a case added without updating the manifest fails a test rather than silently changing a denominator.

sets.title: Regression Set v1
sets.description: The original fourteen questions, first measured in Iteration 3. Frozen: their text, expected answers, keyword requirements and expected evidence must stay byte-identical, because they are the control that makes Iteration 3's numbers comparable to today's. Twelve of the fourteen are answerable from a README or a manifest; only orders q5-oversell-guard and pyflow q6-step-dispatch require reading source. That was a deliberate headroom design, and it is also why the set alone can no longer discriminate between systems — see Challenge Set v2.

sets.title: Challenge Set v2
sets.description: Twenty-four questions added in Iteration 6 against the same two fixtures, weighted deliberately away from documentation. Twenty of the twenty-four have expected evidence that is a source file rather than a README or manifest, and five categories absent from the regression set are covered here for the first time: architecture-inference, behavioral-flow, evidence-precision, competing-evidence and multi-language.

categories.description: Explicitly stated in one relevant source.
Requires joining evidence from more than one location.
Answerable, but not in the wording the question uses.
The question's vocabulary does not occur in the repository at all.
A supported structural conclusion drawn from several files.
Runtime behaviour across a sequence of steps.
An absence claim, which must be established positively rather than by a failed search.
Several files look relevant; only some actually support the claim.
A broad, plausible citation is easy; a precise one exists and is required.
Requires a convention from a language or ecosystem other than the tool's own.

$annotations: Classification for the frozen set only. Challenge questions carry their own metadata inline in their case files; the regression questions cannot, because those two files must stay byte-identical, so their classification lives out here as a sidecar. Keys are caseId/questionId: the regression ids predate the global-uniqueness convention and 'q1-purpose' occurs in both frozen files, so a bare question id is not a key. The classifications are descriptive — they record what each frozen question already tests and are never read by the scorer.

case-001-orders-api/q1-purpose.evidenceRationale: README.md opens by stating that this is the write side of the ordering system.

case-001-orders-api/q2-http-framework.evidenceRationale: express appears in package.json dependencies; a manifest read answers it outright.

case-001-orders-api/q3-event-publication.evidenceRationale: README.md names the order.created topic and package.json carries kafkajs, so both halves are documented.

case-001-orders-api/q4-auth-boundary.evidenceRationale: README.md states that every route needs a bearer token except /health. Challenge q03 asks the same question of the code, where the answer is a middleware ordering fact instead.

case-001-orders-api/q5-oversell-guard.evidenceRationale: The FOR UPDATE row lock is in src/services/inventory.js and the incident report explains why it is there. One of the two regression questions that cannot be answered from documentation.

case-001-orders-api/q6-testing-gap.evidenceRationale: README.md says outright that there are unit tests only and no integration tests; the difficulty is in judging which gap is largest.

case-001-orders-api/q7-api-surface.evidenceRationale: README.md and package.json between them establish an HTTP/Express surface.

case-002-pyflow/q1-purpose.evidenceRationale: README.md describes pyflow as a command-line ETL pipeline runner.

case-002-pyflow/q2-cli-library.evidenceRationale: click is the first entry in the pyproject.toml dependency list.

case-002-pyflow/q3-execution-order.evidenceRationale: README.md states both the topological ordering and the cycle rejection.

case-002-pyflow/q4-state-store.evidenceRationale: Neither README.md nor pyproject.toml says 'this is where run state is recorded' in those words; the answer comes from SQLAlchemy in the manifest plus the state database the readme mentions in passing.

case-002-pyflow/q5-untested-steps.evidenceRationale: README.md names transform as the tested step, which is what makes extract and load the untested ones.

case-002-pyflow/q6-step-dispatch.evidenceRationale: The question says 'mapped to the function that runs it'; the repository says REGISTRY. The other regression question that requires source, and the one that motivated the keyword-mismatch category.

case-002-pyflow/q7-no-external-scheduler.evidenceRationale: README.md states the single-process, sequential execution model, which is positive evidence for the absence of a scheduler rather than a failed search for one.
